newsitem.title: USA: Parents foil Missouri girl's runaway bid.
newsitem.headline: Parents foil Missouri girl's runaway bid.

text.p: A 14-year-old girl who ran away from her Missouri home was picked up by police in California as she was on her way to visit a boy she had met on the Internet, police said on Monday.

Sacramento police said they alerted Greyhound bus officials to keep an eye out for the girl, identified in news reports as Laura Stimpson, after she disappeared on Friday from her home in Raytown, a suburb of Kansas City, Mo.

Authorities believe the girl was on her way to Redwood City, near San Francisco, to meet a 16-year-old boy whom she had met in a chat room on America Online, a company providing access to the Internet.

Greyhound security staff spotted the girl on a San Francisco-bound bus when it stopped in Sacramento on Sunday. They notified Sacramento police who held her until her mother and uncle arrived to collet her, police spokeswoman Pam Alejandre said.
Laura's father, Jay Stimpson, said she began using the online service about a year ago. But as she spent more and more time online, her school grades began to slip.
Stimpson's parents decided to change her password so they could regulate when she was signed onto the service. This reportedly angered the girl, who then began planning to run away from home.
Stimpson's friends knew of her plans to run away, but none of them notified adults until after the girl disappeared.
Stimpson's parents ultimately turned to the chat rooms on America Online to discover who their daughter had been communicating with. They eventually found the California boy's name and called police.

Alejandre warned parents to be aware of their children's computer use. "We've seen far too many cases where someone misrepresents themselves on the Internet," she said, adding that in some of those cases people had ended up in very dangerous situations.
